name: Duruwa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Burrow & Bhattacharya 1953, The Parji Language (archive.org full text READ): Orthography and Phonology chapter contains no stress/accent statement (0 hits for stress/accent in full scanned). No other Duruwa phonology located.

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. 2002. Linguistic Survey of India: Orissa. Kolkata: ORGI.
sources.note: Parji appears only in census tables and one bibliography line; no Parji/Dhurwa grammatical sketch in this volume.

sources.citation: Sjoberg, Andree F. 1971. The Structure of Dravidian Languages. Final Report. Austin: University of Texas / US Office of Education, Bureau of Research (ERIC ED055516). 118 pp.
sources.note: Family-level survey, p. 22 (PDF p. 29): 'Stress occurs automatically on the initial syllable of words and on syllables containing long vowels or ending in a consonant. Intonation is important on the sentence level...'. This is a generalization over Dravidian as a whole; Parji is cited on the same page only for vowel harmony (Pa. cur-ek-en), not for stress.

sources.citation: Burrow, T. & S. Bhattacharya. 1953. The Parji Language: A Dravidian Language of Bastar. Hertford: Stephen Austin and Sons. xii+197 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID Offsite Storage 2233.13 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Chapter I 'Orthography and Phonology' (pp. 1-8, sections 1-10) read in full: phoneme inventory, a/e alternation, auxiliary/anaptyctic vowels, consonant developments, sandhi. Nothing on stress, accent, prominence or intonation; 0 hits for 'stress'/'accent' in both OCRs of the whole book (the only 'emphasi-' hits are about emphatic particles). The scan verdict is confirmed.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page duru1236 (accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Alternate names Dhruva, Dhurwa, Durva, Paraja, Parji, Tagara, Thakara, Tugara; five descriptive refs (Burrow & Bhattacharya 1953; Morton 1978; Joseph 1990; Dutt 1968). No phonology-typed reference.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Duruwa language' (accessed 2026-09-17); cites Krishnamurti 2003: 57 for the phoneme inventory.
sources.note: Vowel and consonant tables only; no information on stress or prosody.

sources.citation: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. 1996. The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. II. Thiruvananthapuram: ISDL.
sources.note: The 'Gond - Dhurwa' entry is listed for Vol. III, which is not online (only Vol. II is on archive.org). Nothing on Parji in Vol. II.

sources.citation: Suvarchala, B. 1992. Central Dravidian Comparative Morphology. New Delhi: Navrang.
sources.note: Brief comparative phonology section (Parji NE/NW/S dialects covered); no stress or accent statement.

sources.citation: Zvelebil, Kamil V. 1990. Dravidian Linguistics: An Introduction. Pondicherry: PILC.
sources.note: Grep of all stress/accent hits: only a remark on vowel loss 'in unaccented non-initial syllables' in Toda and Kota. No Parji stress statement.

sources.citation: Subrahmanyam, P. S. 1983. Dravidian Comparative Phonology. Annamalainagar: Annamalai University.
sources.note: Only historical remarks: reports earlier scholars' 'hypothesis of accent shift from the first syllable to the second in the Central Dravidian languages' and Ramaswami Aiyar's accent-shift explanation of Telugu vowel loss. No synchronic Parji stress statement.

sources.citation: Andronov, M. S. 1970. Dravidian Languages. Moscow: Nauka.
sources.note: Discusses Parji phonemics (Parji-Kolami subgroup) but has no stress/accent statement anywhere (only 'the author must stress').

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.). 1906. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages. Calcutta. Parji section pp. 554-555.
sources.harvard_location: WID Old Widener 3254.1 F; LIN GEN CoPh 5.40; SAN GEN Ud 0010
sources.note: Two-page sketch of 'Parji' treated as a Gondi dialect, from corrupt specimens; 'Pronunciation' paragraph mentions only consonant interchanges (final d/t, n/l). Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. III, entry 'Gond - Dhurwa'. Thiruvananthapuram: ISDL (Vol. II is dated 1996; Vol. III undated in the record seen).
